We're going to see how to sample from both *empirical* and *parametri*c* distributions in R. This is the foundation of *simulation* which is the most important tool in this couse.

## Empirical Dsitributions

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
set.seed(222)
#source("/home/kellymorgan/meds/my_aes/my_theme.R")
# theme_set(my_theme())
theme_set(theme_bw())

soil_cores <- read_csv("exide-soil-cores.csv")
```

`sample()` draws samples from a vector (e.g., a column in a data frame). 

```{r}
pb_ppm_sample <- sample(soil_cores$pb_ppm, size = 50)

# Vizualize thw while distribution
ggplot(soil_cores, aes(pb_ppm)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 20) +
    xlim(0, 1000)

# Visualize just our sample 
tibble(pb_ppm = pb_ppm_sample) |> 
    ggplot(aes(pb_ppm)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 50)
```

`slice_sample()` draws samples from a data frame

```{r}
soil_sample <- soil_cores  |> 
    slice_sample(n =50) # keeps soil_samlpe in dataframe format instead of vector

ggplot(soil_sample, aes(pb_ppm)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 20)
```

## Parametric distributions 

Visualize the PDF with `dnorm()` and other `d___()` functions. When you see a "d__()" function, think PDF: parametric distribution function. 

```{r}
tibble(
    x = seq(-860, 1370, length.out = 1000),
    pdf = dnorm(x, mean = 253, sd = 71) # need to define mean and sd
) |> 
    ggplot(aes(x, pdf)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.5)
```

Draw samples from this distribution with `rnorm()`.

```{r}
normal_sample <- tibble( x = rnorm(25, mean = 254, sd = 371))
ggplot(normal_sample, aes(x)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 100)
```
